summary: Tested the new multi-channel AI Messaging Negotiation Hub (backend /api/communication + frontend /communications) plus regression on Direct Negotiation and Call Center. Backend: 22/22 new pytest cases pass (provider status NOT_CONFIGURED for telegram/whatsapp/instagram with no secret leakage, negotiation start with honest NOT_CONFIGURED delivery, validation 404/400 cases, Telegram inbound webhook running the SHARED engine with quote extraction (780), idempotency (duplicate update_id -> 'duplicate', no extra messages), webhook auth 401 on wrong secret, 'ignored' for bot/non-text, 'no_conversation' + zero writes for unknown chat, above-max quote (1500 vs max 900) -> BUYER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED + within_authority false + AI reply does not accept, approve ACCEPT/REJECT/COUNTER/CLARIFY states, invalid action 400, org isolation 404 on detail/approve/start, and NO orders/purchases/purchase_orders docs created by any communication endpoint). Regression: test_call_center.py 27/27 pass, /api/direct-negotiation/prepare returns a plan. Frontend: login -> 'Comms Hub' nav -> /communications loads, 3 provider chips show NOT CONFIGURED, start modal (mission -> vendor -> telegram -> recipient) creates a conversation, list + detail with metric tiles and NEGOBUY AI outreach bubble marked NOT_CONFIGURED, and the approval panel Accept flow flips stage to APPROVED with 'Decision: ACCEPT'. No console errors, no error elements.

minor.issue: Inbound conversation lookup is db.conversations.find_one({channel, recipient}) with no organization/mission scoping and no ordering — if the same chat id/phone is used by two orgs (or two missions), the inbound message and the engine turn can be attributed to an arbitrary/wrong conversation (cross-org attribution risk). Suggest scoping+sorting by last_activity and, ideally, per-org provider identity.

When the provider is NOT_CONFIGURED the conversation comm_state is set to 'OUTREACH_FAILED' — semantically this is not a failure but 'not sent / provider not configured'. A distinct state (e.g. OUTREACH_PENDING_SETUP) would be more honest and avoids the misleading 'OUTREACH FAILED' badge in the UI.

ui_bugs.issue: Stage value truncates: 'BUYER APPROVAL ...' — tile width too small for the longest state labels

issues: List rows show only vendor name + state + quote; channel and recipient (chat id) are not shown, so multiple conversations with the same vendor on different recipients are indistinguishable
Rows labelled 'OUTREACH FAILED' for the NOT_CONFIGURED case read as an error to the user (see backend minor issue)

action_items: Scope the inbound webhook conversation lookup (org/mission) and sort by last_activity to avoid mis-attribution when a chat id is reused.
Rename the NOT_CONFIGURED outreach state away from 'OUTREACH_FAILED' (backend + UI badge).
Widen/wrap the Stage metric tile so 'BUYER APPROVAL REQUIRED' is fully visible; add channel + recipient to conversation list rows.
critical_code_review_comments: communication_service._handle_inbound: conversation match on {channel, recipient} only — add organization/mission scoping and deterministic ordering.
Idempotency via comm_events._id = provider event id is correct and verified; keep event ids channel-prefixed (already done) to avoid cross-provider collisions.
No purchase/order writes were found in any /api/communication path — verified empirically by counting orders/purchases/purchase_orders before and after inbound + ACCEPT.
